argument.issue: Did the Officer unreasonably reject the new evidence under paragraph 113(a) of IRPA?
argument.claim: The Officer unreasonably rejected new evidence by not engaging with its credibility, relevance, or materiality.
argument.quote: The Officer’s concern was authentication. But the Officer did not say what further proof was needed, and did not engage with the Applicant’s affidavit.

support.ref: Raza v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2007 FCA 385
Applicant’s affidavit, arrest warrant, news reports

argument.weak_spot: The other side may argue the Officer reasonably doubted the authenticity of the documents and explained why.

best_match.label: same_question
best_match.issue: Should the RAD admit the new evidence submitted by the Appellant under Section 110(4) IRPA?
best_match.quoted_paragraph: Is this affidavit "new"? The RAD finds that it is not new, as it deals only with the recorded record of the hearing which occurred on May 16, 2014. There is nothing new in the affidavit and the content of the affidavit itself is not material because it only reiterates what was on the official record. This affidavit will be disallowed.

argument.issue: Did the Officer breach procedural fairness by making credibility findings without a hearing, contrary to paragraph 113(b) of IRPA and section 167 of the IRPR?
argument.claim: The Officer made a credibility finding without a hearing, contrary to the prescribed factors in section 167 of the IRPR.
argument.quote: The Officer here said the warrant “could not be authenticated”, which is, in substance, a finding that the Applicant is not credible. All three of the section 167 factors are met.

support.ref: Singh v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2016 FCA 96

argument.weak_spot: The other side may argue the Officer did not make a credibility finding but rather assessed sufficiency of evidence.

best_match.label: same_question
best_match.issue: Did the RAD breach procedural fairness by making new negative credibility findings without opportunity to respond?
best_match.quoted_paragraph: In Koffi, above, Justice Catherine M. Kane stated that even if the RAD made independent findings of credibility against an applicant, without putting it before the applicant and giving him or her the opportunity to make submissions, the RAD’s decision may still be reasonable. argument.issue: Did the Officer apply the correct legal tests under sections 96 and 97 of IRPA?
argument.claim: The Officer failed to separately assess the section 96 and 97 tests and treated the matter solely as a credibility issue.
argument.quote: The Officer did not assess either test separately and treated the question as one of credibility.

support.ref: Adjei v Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration), [1989] 2 FC 680 (CA)
Li v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2005 FCA 1

argument.weak_spot: The other side may argue the Officer’s reasons, read as a whole, addressed the required legal tests.
